source.citation: Penas E, Uberti F, Baviera G, Di Lorenzo C, Restani P. Clinical monosensitivity to salmon and rainbow trout: a case report. Pediatr Allergy Immunol 2014;25(1):98-100.

patient_description: 14-year-old boy, cow's-milk allergy since infancy. First salmon reaction at age 4 (rash, lip edema) after appetizers with smoked salmon (SPT/prick-to-prick to fish negative at that time). Reaction to broiled salmon 2 years later. Severe throat itching after broiled rainbow trout at age 11. Safely consumes cod, halibut, anchovy, tuna, mackerel (one reaction to fish sticks made of cod, hypothesized salmon cross-contamination).

verification.notes: CRITICAL stress-test case: sequence-similarity-based tools would likely predict cross-reactivity from parvalbumin markers (Sal s/Onc m positive), but the actual IgE-binding driver is beta-enolase, NOT parvalbumin -- the immunoblot explicitly shows no IgE binding to the parvalbumin band itself. A naive similarity predictor should be expected to under- or mis-perform on this case; use it to characterize failure modes, not just successes. No OFC performed.

double_mixed_note: 6 positive (salmonids + percids: brook trout, brown trout, Danube salmon, rainbow trout, European perch, pikeperch) + 6 negative (Northern pike, Wels catfish, common carp, tench, European eel, sterlet) = QUALIFIES, and is the single richest double-mixed patient found across all searches so far. Verbatim from source: 'P44 was positive to parvalbumins from salmonids and percids and negative to all others.'

verification.notes: Full text read; positive/negative assignment per component verbatim from Results/Discussion text. Exact kUA/L values per component are in Figure S5 of the supplement, which was not retrievable in this session -- value fields left null rather than estimated. Positivity threshold for the whole study is 0.3 kUA/L. Each parvalbumin was confirmed as a distinct species protein by LC-MS/MS per the source, but note not all of these freshwater species have official IUIS allergen codes (e.g. rainbow trout Onc m 1 and common carp Cyp c 1 are IUIS-coded; several others are not) -- flag this if your pipeline requires IUIS-coded names specifically.
